body:
wylie goodman wrote:

>Dear Una Fans,

Don't let the newsgroup name fool you. Not everyone here is a fan. There are
varying levels of support for TK here. These are my personal answers to your
questions.

>1.    Do people believe T.K. is mentally ill?  If so, does this lessen
>
> in any way your feelings regarding him and his actions?

I do not believe that TK is a paranoid schizophrenic. I do believe that he
suffered from depression, as so many other people do. I feel sorry for his
loneliness, abhor his violence, and believe that Industrial Society and its
Future raises some important questions that deserve a more prominent place in
our public discourse.

>2.    Do people share T.K.'s view that technology is ruling and
>ruining our lives?  If so, why and why use the internet to have this
> discussion?

It is my very unscientific observation that many people share at least some of
TK's views. Unbridled technology, or technology for technology's sake, without
sufficient thought as to its consequences is a dangerous thing. On the other
hand, the internet is one of the few places where one may excercise one's right
to free speech on important topics. Other forums such as letters to the local
newspaper, etc. must be approved by an editor. And even that involves
technology!

See also paragraph 202 of the manifesto: "It would be hopeless for
revolutionaries to try to attack the system without using SOME modern
technology. If nothing else they must use the communications media to spread
their message."

>3..    Do people consider T.K. an anarchist?

John Zerzan, a prominent anarchist writer does. You might want to check out
"Anarchy" magazine, which you can find at a good bookstore or newsstand.

> 4.    Would people view T.K. as less effective if he had only
>published his words (The Manifesto) rather than acted on them via deeds
>  (Sending mailbombs)?

TK's use of bombs has probably made him less effective, since so many people
refuse to read the manifesto because of his deeds. Yet of course, I wouldn't
have read it if it weren't for the Unabomber case! The idea of how TK could
have more effectively gotten his message out has been discussed before. If
someone can remember the name of one of those threads, you might want to look
it up in DejaNews.

>5.    What do people think is/are the element (s) that allow two
>individuals to have
>fairly similar  life experiences [equal parts love and trauma (i.e.
>jilted relationship, etc.)]
>but that leads one to sublimate those experiences into art and the other
>to
>turn them outward into acts of violence?

Wow, if I knew the answer to this one, I would have a very successful practice
as a psychologist:-)

As far as a live Unabomber discussion, I don't know how the others feel. I like
the newsgroup format for this topic. It allows for more depth. But, I'm not
into chat rooms. If you wanted to, you could probably do a slide show type
thing of various threads.

Good luck with your project!

And, I'm curious too - what got you interested?
